evals.prompt: Add comments to retry_queue.h and retry_queue.cc: the class, the functions, and the member variables all need appropriate comments. Modify the files directly.
evals.expected_output: Contract comments live at the declarations in the .h (third-person declarative); the .cc only explains implementation choices and does not duplicate the header comments. Ownership of the raw payload pointer, NextReadyAt's -1.0 sentinel, MarkFailed's nullopt ambiguity (unknown id vs dropped task), and the units of base_delay_s_ are all documented. No Author: lines, no comments that restate the code.

evals.prompt: Review the comment quality of session_store.h and session_store.cc. Write a report listing every problem you find, ordered by severity. Do not change the code yet.
evals.expected_output: Report ordered by harm: first the comment/behavior contradictions (Get() claims to return an empty string but throws out_of_range; a nonexistent timeout_s parameter is documented), then missing contracts (the negative-ttl never-expires sentinel, Get()'s evict-on-read side effect), then placement problems (.h comment duplicated into the .cc), and finally noise (Author: line, restating comments, commented-out code, malformed TODO, wrong /* notify */ argument-comment form, imperative mood).

evals.prompt: Write a C++ token-bucket rate limiter: rate_limiter.h and rate_limiter.cc, with a TokenBucket class supporting a blocking Acquire(n) and a non-blocking TryAcquire(n). Comments must be complete.
evals.expected_output: The class comment states the purpose and the thread-safety guarantee; every public method declaration in the .h carries a third-person contract comment (blocking semantics, timeout, return-value meaning, units); .cc comments explain implementation rationale only; no restating comments; any bare literal argument uses the /*param=*/ form.
